source_text: Condicio praesentium temporum etiam hanc admonitionem provocat nostram, non oportere nos mirari super haereses istas, sive quia sunt, futurae enim praenuntiabantur, sive quia fidem quorundam subvertunt, ad hoc enim sunt, ut fides habendo temptationem haberet etiam probationem. Vane ergo et inconsiderato plerique hoc ipso scandalizantur, quod tantum haereses valeant. Quantum, si non fuissent? Cum quid sortitum est ut omnimodo sit, causam accipit ob quam sit. Haec vim consequitur per quam sit, ne esse non possit.
thought_title: Heresies were predicted and serve to test faith
orientation: Tertullian opens the treatise by telling believers they should not be shocked that heresies exist or that they overturn some people's faith.
pass_a_gloss: The condition of the present times also calls forth this warning of ours, that we ought not to be astonished at these heresies, either because they exist, for they were foretold as future, or because they overturn the faith of some, for they exist for this purpose, so that faith, by having temptation, might also have testing. Therefore vainly and thoughtlessly most people are scandalized by this very thing, that heresies have so much power. How much would they have, if they had not existed? When something has been allotted to exist in every way, it receives a cause for which it exists. This obtains the force through which it exists, so that it cannot not exist.

lemmas.gloss: are scandalized, are made to stumble

choices.why: Fixed glossary term for factions choosing their own doctrine against the apostolic faith.
The Christian faith as received from the apostles; kept as 'faith' to match the treatise's core contrast between faith and heresy.
Renders the testing circumstance that faith undergoes; keeps the moral trial sense Tertullian develops.
Distinguishes the proving of faith from the temptation that occasions it.
Preserves the biblical term for being made to stumble, which Tertullian uses deliberately.
Keeps the sense of divine or providential assignment, not mere chance.

pass_b_english: The state of the present times also prompts this warning of mine: we should not be astonished at these heresies. We should not be astonished that they exist, for their coming was foretold. Nor should we be astonished that they overturn the faith of some, since they exist for this very purpose: so that faith, by undergoing temptation, might also undergo testing. So it is in vain and without reflection that many people are scandalized by the very fact that heresies have so much power. How much power would they have if they did not exist? When something has been allotted to exist in every way, it receives a cause for which it exists. It gains the force through which it exists, so that it cannot fail to exist.

problems.quote: When something has been allotted to exist in every way, it receives a cause for which it exists. It gains the force through which it exists, so that it cannot not exist.
problems.why: Tautological and abstract; 'cannot not exist' is awkward double negative.
problems.fix: Simplify: 'it cannot fail to exist' or 'its existence is necessary.'

edits.old: so that it cannot not exist.
edits.new: so that it cannot fail to exist.

fixed: Changed 'cannot not exist' to 'cannot fail to exist' to remove the awkward double negative while preserving the source meaning 'ne esse non possit'.

polish.changed: Clarified the opening by breaking the long sentence into shorter, more natural units, and smoothed the final abstract sentence to avoid the awkward double negative while preserving the exact claim.
